title: Derived extension from abelian towers and its normalized integer unit
statement: For a scheme T and any system B of commutative ring sheaves on its pro-etale site, with the actual module-system category, forgetful-functor specification and integer generator of [def-sp-tower-class-systems], there exist a Reduction r [def-sp-tower-class-reduction] and an isomorphism from its derived extension of the degree-zero constant integer tower to the degree-zero coefficient unit. The adjunct of this isomorphism, followed by the canonical single-functor comparison for forgetting, is the degree-zero integerGenerator. This asserts no Kummer or root-tower comparison and requires no prime or invertibility hypothesis.

proof.text: Use the proved ordinary integral-tower scalar presentation to obtain R, phi, the additive equivalence e, its source-unit isomorphism, the literal exact Forget functor, and the normalized ordinary adjunction/unit comparison for every prescribed scalar-extension functor.

source.place: clause (2), simultaneous integral reduction; IntegralUnitReduction proof steps 1 and 3, ordinary tensor and integer-unit calculation

proof.text: Take the proved independent-universe change-of-rings cochain model for phi, retaining its ordinary functor and preservation of quasi-isomorphisms between K-flat complexes. Define a resolving class of abelian-tower complexes by requiring that its image under e be isomorphic to a K-flat complex. Lift K-flat resolutions through the cochain equivalence; exactness preserves their quasi-isomorphisms. Conjugate a quasi-isomorphism between these models by the chosen isomorphisms and use scalar-extension K-flat invariance. Apply the proved resolving-class derived-adjunction theorem. Its transpose equation, followed by the canonical restriction factor, gives exactly DerivedExtension.transpose.

source.place: clause (2), simultaneous integral reduction; IntegralUnitReduction proof steps 1 and 3, ordinary tensor and integer-unit calculation

proof.text: The ordinary unit module is flat because right tensor with it is naturally isomorphic to the identity. The proved flat-single normalization makes its single complex K-flat. The ordinary source-unit isomorphism therefore places the actual integer single complex in the resolving class, so its derived comparison epsilon is invertible. Compose epsilon with the single-complex ordinary multiplication isomorphism to obtain a. The cochain adjunction on single complexes is the single of the ordinary adjunction, as checked in degree zero and by zero-source uniqueness in every other degree. Apply the retained transpose formula and the canonical exact-forgetting single comparison. The ordinary generator equality from the scalar presentation proves sourceNormalization for precisely integerGenerator.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_integralUnitReduction (T : Scheme.{u})
    (B : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology T) CommRingCat.{u + 1}) :
    ∃ (r : Reduction T B)
      (a : r.derived.obj ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (Ab T) 0).obj (integers T)) ≅
        unit T B),
      r.model.sourceNormalization a (integerGenerator T B r.forget)
